audit_status.source_base: Hebrew source via Sefaria with source/English versification reconciliation; public-domain KJV familiar comparison
audit_status.review_note: Drafted from the Hebrew MT (Chronicles) aligned to KJV verse numbering; preserves name-variants (Huram/Hiram), 'algum' wood, numeric uncertainty (666), and the idiom 'no more spirit' — YHWH rendered as required. Pending witness review for a few lexical and numeric items.

verses.restored: When the queen of Sheba heard the fame of Solomon, she came to test Solomon with ḥidot (riddles) at Jerusalem, with a very great company and camels bearing spices and much gold and precious stones; she came to Solomon and spoke with him about all that was in her heart.

familiar.text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.

verses.restored: Solomon answered all her questions; there was no matter from Solomon that he did not tell her.

familiar.text: And Solomon told her all her questions: and there was nothing hid from Solomon which he told her not.

verses.restored: When the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon and the house he had built,

familiar.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, and the house that he had built,

verses.restored: and the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his officers and their apparel, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the ascent by which he went up into the house of YHWH — there was no more spirit in her.

familiar.text: And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel; his cupbearers also, and their apparel; and his ascent by which he went up into the house of the LORD; there was no more spirit in her.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Hebrew idiom rendered literally; 'no more spirit in her' (נֶפֶשׁ/רוּחַ) preserved as ambiguous emotional/physiological response.

verses.restored: She said to the king, 'It was true what I heard in my land concerning your deeds and concerning your wisdom.'

familiar.text: And she said to the king, It was a true report which I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom:

verses.restored: But I did not believe their words until I came and my eyes had seen; and behold, half the report had not been told me — you have added to the hearing.

familiar.text: Howbeit I believed not their words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the one half of the greatness of thy wisdom was not told me: for thou exceedest the fame that I heard.

verses.restored: Blessed are your men, and blessed are these your servants who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom.

familiar.text: Happy are thy men, and happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and hear thy wisdom.

verses.restored: Blessed be YHWH your God, who delighted in you to set you on his throne to be king for YHWH your God; because your God loved Israel to establish them for ever, therefore he made you king over them to do justice and righteousness.

familiar.text: Blessed be the LORD thy God, which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for the LORD thy God: because thy God loved Israel, to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice.

verses.restored: She gave the king 120 talents of gold, and a very great store of spices and precious stones; there had not been such spices as those which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

familiar.text: And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices great abundance, and precious stones: neither was there any such spice as the queen of Sheba gave king Solomon.

verses.restored: And the servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir brought algum-wood and precious stones.

familiar.text: And the servants also of Huram, and the servants of Solomon, which brought gold from Ophir, brought algum trees and precious stones.

notes.title: short
notes.body: Name preserved as Huram (חוּרָם); variant readings (Hiram) exist in other witnesses.

verses.restored: The king made of the algum-wood mesillot (carved work/terraces) for the house of YHWH and for the king's house, and harps and psalteries for the singers; nothing like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.

familiar.text: And the king made of the algum trees terraces to the house of the LORD, and to the king’s palace, and harps and psalteries for singers: and there were none such seen before in the land of Judah.

notes.title: short
notes.body: 'mesillot' left literal (מְסִילוֹת) — translation choice reflects textual uncertainty about architectural term.

verses.restored: King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire which she asked, besides what she had brought to the king; then she turned and went away to her own land she and her servants.

familiar.text: And king Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which she had brought unto the king. So she turned, and went away to her own land, she and her servants.

verses.restored: The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold.

familiar.text: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold;

notes.title: short
notes.body: Numeric reading preserved from MT; variant traditions differ (see LXX and other witnesses).

verses.restored: Besides the traders and merchants who brought, and all the kings of Arabia and governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.

familiar.text: Beside that which chapmen and merchants brought. And all the kings of Arabia and governors of the country brought gold and silver to Solomon.

verses.restored: King Solomon made two hundred shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one shield.

familiar.text: And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one target.

verses.restored: And three hundred shields made he of beaten gold; three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

familiar.text: And three hundred shields made he of beaten gold: three hundred shekels of gold went to one shield. And the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.

verses.restored: Moreover the king made a great ivory throne and overlaid it with pure gold.

familiar.text: Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.

verses.restored: There were six steps to the throne, and a footstool of gold fastened to the throne; on each side of the seat there were stays, and two lions standing beside the stays.

familiar.text: And there were six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne, and stays on each side of the sitting place, and two lions standing by the stays:

verses.restored: Twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps; there was no one like it made in any kingdom.

familiar.text: And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps. There was not the like made in any kingdom.

verses.restored: All the drinking vessels of King Solomon were of gold; all the vessels in the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; silver was not considered of value in the days of Solomon.

familiar.text: And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: none were of silver; it was not any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon.

verses.restored: For the king's ships went to Tarshish with Huram's servants; once every three years came the ships of Tarshish, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

familiar.text: For the king’s ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Huram: every three years once came the ships of Tarshish bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

verses.restored: King Solomon excelled all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.

familiar.text: And king Solomon passed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.

verses.restored: All the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom which God had put in his heart.

familiar.text: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that God had put in his heart.

verses.restored: They brought every man his present: vessels of silver, vessels of gold, robes, armor, spices, horses, and mules, yearly.

familiar.text: And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and raiment, harness, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.

verses.restored: Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; and he placed them in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen; whom he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem.

verses.restored: He reigned over all the kings from the river unto the land of the Philistines, and unto the border of Egypt.

familiar.text: And he reigned over all the kings from the river even unto the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt.

verses.restored: The king made silver in Jerusalem as common as stones, and he caused the cedars to be as plentiful as the sycomores that are in the lowland.

familiar.text: And the king made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar trees made he as the sycomore trees that are in the low plains in abundance.

notes.title: short
notes.body: 'Silver as stones' is an idiom in the Hebrew text preserved literally; interpretive options vary.

verses.restored: They brought horses to Solomon out of Egypt and out of all lands.

familiar.text: And they brought unto Solomon horses out of Egypt, and out of all lands.

verses.restored: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, are they not written in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat?

notes.title: short
notes.body: Multiple prophetic sources named; Chronicles preserves the cross-references though witness forms vary (Iddo/Yeddo).

verses.restored: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

familiar.text: And Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

verses.restored: Then Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father; and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

familiar.text: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

translation_notes: Divine name יהוה rendered consistently as YHWH.
Numeric reading 666 (v.13) flagged — MT tradition and LXX/other witnesses differ; preserve ambiguity.
Names and technical terms preserved (חוּרָם / 'Huram', עֲצֵי אַלְגּוּמִּים / 'algum') and left for later lexical identification.
safety_note: Contains celebration of wealth, power, and political dominance; preserves morally difficult material and ambiguous wording for scholarly review.
